questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: In Genesis 41, what links Joseph’s interpretation of Pharaoh’s dreams to his administrative proposal?
options: He recommends storing grain during plentiful years before the predicted famine.
He recommends distributing all grain in the plentiful years without keeping a reserve.
He recommends importing grain only after the famine has exhausted local supplies.
He recommends leaving storage entirely to Pharaoh’s dream interpreters without administrators.
questions.answer: He recommends storing grain during plentiful years before the predicted famine.
questions.explanation: The predicted sequence of abundance and famine leads Joseph to propose advance storage and supervision.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: In Genesis 45, Joseph invites his brothers to come closer during the disclosure of his identity. What best explains the significance of this scene?
options: Joseph keeps his identity secret and questions them only through an interpreter.
He is disclosing his identity and addressing brothers distressed by his presence.
Joseph accuses Benjamin of stealing before ordering the brothers to fetch him.
Joseph negotiates a price for selling the brothers to another official.
questions.answer: He is disclosing his identity and addressing brothers distressed by his presence.
questions.explanation: Joseph identifies himself, asks about his father and reassures his alarmed brothers; the scene is one of recognition and reconciliation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: Moses’ objection that he is not an effective speaker is answered in Exodus 4 partly by
options: The appointment of Joshua as his spokesman before Pharaoh.
The appointment of Jethro to deliver the message in his place.
the appointment of Aaron to speak with him.
The appointment of Caleb to speak while Moses remains in Midian.
questions.answer: the appointment of Aaron to speak with him.
questions.explanation: Aaron is to serve as spokesman, while Moses receives and communicates the message.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: In Numbers 27, why does Moses request the appointment of a successor?
options: So authority will pass automatically to the oldest of his sons.
So the congregation can remain in the wilderness without anyone leading it.
So the priesthood can be transferred permanently to Pharaoh’s family.
So the community will not be left without leadership.
questions.answer: So the community will not be left without leadership.
questions.explanation: Moses asks for someone to lead the congregation, using the image of sheep without a shepherd.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: Deborah’s role in Judges 4 most directly challenges which assumption?
options: That women are absent from every leadership role in the biblical narrative.
That Barak participates in the campaign.
That a recognised judge can hear disputes brought by Israelites.
That the narrative includes conflict with an opposing army.
questions.answer: That women are absent from every leadership role in the biblical narrative.
questions.explanation: Deborah is identified as a prophetess and judge who summons and instructs Barak.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: In 1 Samuel 15, Samuel rejects Saul’s attempt to justify retaining livestock for sacrifice because
options: Samuel teaches that livestock can never be offered in any worship.
ritual offerings do not excuse disobedience to the command given.
Saul had been instructed to make himself king of Egypt.
The dispute concerns only the market price of sheep.
questions.answer: ritual offerings do not excuse disobedience to the command given.
questions.explanation: Samuel’s response contrasts obedience with an attempted sacrificial justification for disobedience.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: What makes Rehoboam’s reply in 1 Kings 12 a failure of responsive leadership?
options: He reduces the burden immediately in response to the elders’ counsel.
He delays his reply until the northern tribes have already accepted his policy.
He promises a heavier burden after the people request relief.
He replaces the requested relief with a plan agreed unanimously by elders and people.
questions.answer: He promises a heavier burden after the people request relief.
questions.explanation: Rehoboam follows harsh advice and threatens increased burdens, contributing to division.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Relate prophetic critiques and reform narratives to justice and accountability.
questions.prompt: In the Naboth narrative, why is the use of false witnesses especially serious?
options: Naboth had volunteered to sell the vineyard at the offered price.
The witnesses are merely discussing the vineyard’s soil quality.
The dispute ends with Naboth choosing a different vineyard freely.
Legal and religious procedures are manipulated to seize another person’s inheritance.
questions.answer: Legal and religious procedures are manipulated to seize another person’s inheritance.
questions.explanation: False accusations lead to Naboth’s death and enable Ahab’s seizure of his vineyard.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Relate prophetic critiques and reform narratives to justice and accountability.
questions.prompt: Gehazi’s conduct after Naaman’s healing is condemned because he
options: uses deception to obtain gifts that Elisha had refused.
He accepts a gift openly after Elisha authorises him to do so.
He refuses payment but asks Naaman to return to the Jordan.
He reports truthfully that Naaman insisted on thanking Elisha personally.
questions.answer: uses deception to obtain gifts that Elisha had refused.
questions.explanation: Gehazi falsely attributes a request to Elisha and then lies about his own actions.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Relate prophetic critiques and reform narratives to justice and accountability.
questions.prompt: Amos 5 criticises religious celebrations when they coexist with
options: honest judging and concern for the poor.
the denial of justice and oppression of the vulnerable.
fair treatment in public dealings.
repentance expressed through changed conduct.
questions.answer: the denial of justice and oppression of the vulnerable.
questions.explanation: The passage rejects worship detached from justice rather than condemning justice as a substitute for wrongdoing.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Relate prophetic critiques and reform narratives to justice and accountability.
questions.prompt: Hosea 6:6 gives priority to which contrast?
options: Military expansion over covenant faithfulness.
Expensive ceremonies over mercy.
Steadfast love and knowledge of God over sacrifice alone.
Royal power over the knowledge of God.
questions.answer: Steadfast love and knowledge of God over sacrifice alone.
questions.explanation: Hosea criticises ritual unaccompanied by faithful relationship and steadfast love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: At Jesus’ baptism in Matthew 3, the heavenly declaration chiefly identifies
options: John’s replacement of Jesus as the promised Son.
The appointment of Jesus to the Jerusalem high priesthood.
The removal of every future test from Jesus’ ministry.
Jesus’ relationship to God and divine approval.
questions.answer: Jesus’ relationship to God and divine approval.
questions.explanation: The voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son and expresses approval; the narrative does not say temptation has ended.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: In Matthew 4, Jesus’ refusal to jump from the temple demonstrates that
options: scriptural language should not be used to justify testing God.
any quotation of scripture makes an action right.
faith requires deliberately creating danger to demand rescue.
the tempter had offered no scriptural argument.
questions.answer: scriptural language should not be used to justify testing God.
questions.explanation: The temptation uses scripture, but Jesus answers with the prohibition against putting God to the test.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: In the call of the fishermen in Mark 1, which response is emphasised?
options: Remaining at work until Jesus guarantees financial security.
Leaving their previous work to follow Jesus.
Requesting formal posts before agreeing to follow him.
Following John while postponing a response to Jesus.
questions.answer: Leaving their previous work to follow Jesus.
questions.explanation: The account stresses their prompt response to Jesus’ call rather than a negotiation for status.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: The servant forgiven a large debt in Matthew 18 is later condemned mainly because he
options: cannot calculate the original debt accurately.
forgives his fellow servant before asking the king.
refuses to extend mercy after receiving mercy himself.
asks another servant to keep proper records.
questions.answer: refuses to extend mercy after receiving mercy himself.
questions.explanation: The parable highlights the inconsistency between receiving forgiveness and acting mercilessly towards another debtor.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: In Gethsemane, Jesus’ prayer in Matthew 26 holds together
options: complete indifference to suffering and a desire for public office.
a denial that any suffering is possible and a call for revenge.
a command that the disciples arrest the chief priests.
distress and submission to the Father’s will.
questions.answer: distress and submission to the Father’s will.
questions.explanation: Jesus expresses anguish while yielding his request to the Father’s will.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: After Peter’s denials in Luke 22, what event immediately leads him to remember Jesus’ warning?
options: The Lord turns and looks at him after the cock crows.
The tearing of the temple curtain as Peter watches.
The darkness at the crucifixion before Peter is questioned.
The return of Judas to the chief priests during Peter’s trial.
questions.answer: The Lord turns and looks at him after the cock crows.
questions.explanation: The look and cockcrow recall the earlier warning, and Peter goes out and weeps.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain decisions and community challenges in the early church.
questions.prompt: What practical problem leads to the selection of the Seven in Acts 6?
options: A dispute about replacing Judas among the Twelve.
Some widows are being overlooked in the daily distribution.
A request that the apostles cease preaching to Gentiles.
A shortage of candidates who had witnessed Jesus’ baptism.
questions.answer: Some widows are being overlooked in the daily distribution.
questions.explanation: The complaint concerns unequal treatment in support distribution; the community appoints suitable people to address it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain decisions and community challenges in the early church.
questions.prompt: According to Peter in Acts 5, what makes Ananias’s action blameworthy?
options: He refuses a rule that every member must sell land.
He truthfully states he has kept part of the sale money.
He lies about the proceeds rather than being required to surrender property compulsorily.
He asks the apostles whether property may remain unsold.
questions.answer: He lies about the proceeds rather than being required to surrender property compulsorily.
questions.explanation: Peter states that the property and proceeds were under Ananias’s control; deception is the issue.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain decisions and community challenges in the early church.
questions.prompt: Acts 2 presents the crowd’s amazement at Pentecost as connected with
options: All listeners abandoning their native languages to learn Aramaic first.
Only Jerusalem residents being permitted to listen.
The crowd understanding solely through a written translation supplied later.
hearing the speakers in the listeners’ own languages.
questions.answer: hearing the speakers in the listeners’ own languages.
questions.explanation: The passage names visitors from many places and describes their surprise at hearing familiar languages.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain decisions and community challenges in the early church.
questions.prompt: Peter’s defence in Acts 11 appeals to the Spirit’s coming upon Gentiles to explain why
options: he should not obstruct God’s acceptance of them.
Gentile acceptance depended first on obtaining Roman citizenship.
The Spirit’s gift should be withheld until every critic approved the visit.
The event had no bearing on questions of fellowship with Gentiles.
questions.answer: he should not obstruct God’s acceptance of them.
questions.explanation: Peter recounts the events as evidence that the Gentiles received the same divine gift.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply the teaching of James and 1 Peter while retaining its textual context.
questions.prompt: A person offers kind words to a hungry believer but refuses available food. Which teaching in James 2 most directly challenges this?

A claim of faith without practical help is inadequate.
Only public speaking can express faith.
Material needs are irrelevant to the example James gives.
questions.answer: A claim of faith without practical help is inadequate.
questions.explanation: James uses unmet needs for clothing and food to show the emptiness of words without action.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

the example of impartial treatment it recommends.
partiality inconsistent with the community’s faith.
proof that wealth determines moral worth.
questions.answer: partiality inconsistent with the community’s faith.
questions.explanation: James condemns preferential treatment based on outward wealth.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply the teaching of James and 1 Peter while retaining its textual context.
questions.prompt: James 1 links careful listening with restraint in speaking and anger because
options: anger always proves that a person has listened accurately.
speaking first makes evidence unnecessary.
any disagreement cancels the duty to listen.
human anger does not produce the righteousness God desires.
questions.answer: human anger does not produce the righteousness God desires.
questions.explanation: The passage connects readiness to listen with restrained speech and anger.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply the teaching of James and 1 Peter while retaining its textual context.
questions.prompt: Which leadership practice fits 1 Peter 5:2–3?
options: Leading willingly by example rather than dominating those entrusted to one’s care.
Using office principally for dishonest gain.
Treating responsibility as permission to humiliate members.
Avoiding all personal example while demanding compliance.
questions.answer: Leading willingly by example rather than dominating those entrusted to one’s care.
questions.explanation: The exhortation contrasts willing, exemplary oversight with exploitation and domination.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret humanity’s place and responsibility in the Genesis creation narrative.
questions.prompt: In Genesis 1, the description of humanity’s responsibility towards other living things most directly introduces a theme of

stewardship within creation.
the absence of any responsibility towards other creatures.
creation’s dependence on human beings for its initial existence.
questions.answer: stewardship within creation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

options: He denies that the people have broken any command.
He asks that Aaron’s calf become the permanent object of worship.
He pleads for the people despite their wrongdoing.
He offers himself as the ruler who should be worshipped instead.
questions.answer: He pleads for the people despite their wrongdoing.
questions.explanation: Moses appeals to God’s purposes and promises rather than denying the offence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.
questions.prompt: In Joshua 1:7–9, courage is linked especially with

avoiding responsibility until no difficulty remains.
measuring success only by possession of military equipment.
faithfulness to the instruction given, not mere self-confidence.
questions.answer: faithfulness to the instruction given, not mere self-confidence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret leadership decisions and consequences in prescribed Old Testament narratives.

That the repeated call is an instruction from Saul.
That Samuel should bring the ark to the battlefield immediately.
That the voice is one of Eli’s sons asking for a sacrifice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

will not strike the Lord’s anointed to obtain the kingdom.
He considers the spear worthless as evidence of access to Saul.
He accepts Abner’s offer to surrender Saul’s army.

questions.prompt: In Solomon’s judgement between the two women, what reveals the true mother’s concern?

Her claim to own a larger house.
Her willingness to surrender her claim so the child may live.
Her ability to pay the king a higher fee.
questions.answer: Her willingness to surrender her claim so the child may live.
questions.explanation: Her compassion for the living child exposes a concern deeper than winning the dispute.

questions.prompt: Using Genesis 41:25–36, explain how Joseph’s proposal combines interpretation with practical preparation. Develop four points.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: Joseph interprets the paired dreams as one message, connecting their images rather than treating them as unrelated events. He identifies plentiful years followed by famine, so present abundance does not justify assuming permanent security. He recommends appointing a discerning administrator and overseers, linking a forecast to organised responsibility. He proposes collecting and storing grain during abundance for later scarcity; the plan translates knowledge into preparation rather than panic.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret Jesus’ actions and teaching in their stated Synoptic Gospel contexts.
questions.prompt: Analyse the relationship between mercy received and mercy shown in Matthew 18:23–35. Develop four connected points.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: The first servant faces an overwhelming debt and depends on the king’s compassion rather than his ability to repay. The king releases him from the debt, establishing mercy as a gift already received. The servant then uses coercion against a fellow servant despite a plea resembling his own, revealing inconsistent treatment. The king condemns that refusal of compassion; the concluding application calls for heartfelt forgiveness rather than merely demanding it for oneself.
questions.explanation: Credit other accurate, relevant explanations grounded in the specified text. Award each distinct idea once. The guide is original practice material, not an official examiner scheme.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain decisions and community challenges in the early church.
questions.prompt: How does the response to the distribution complaint in Acts 6:1–6 combine fairness and responsible organisation? Explain four points.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: The complaint identifies overlooked Hellenistic widows, so the issue is an actual pattern of unequal provision rather than an abstract argument. The apostles involve the community in selecting suitable people instead of ignoring the affected group’s concern. Good reputation, the Spirit and wisdom are stated qualifications, connecting practical service with character. Commissioning the Seven assigns responsibility while allowing the apostles to continue prayer and ministry of the word; differentiated roles support the same community.
questions.explanation: Credit other accurate, relevant explanations grounded in the specified text. Award each distinct idea once. The guide is original practice material, not an official examiner scheme.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply the teaching of James and 1 Peter while retaining its textual context.
questions.prompt: Using James 2:1–9, explain four reasons why preferential seating based on wealth conflicts with the passage’s teaching.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: The rich visitor is honoured for visible clothing while the poor visitor is demeaned, so judgement rests on outward status. The unequal seating exposes discriminatory distinctions within an assembly that professes faith. James challenges the assumption that wealth establishes a person’s worth before God by recalling God’s concern for the poor. The duty to love one’s neighbour is inconsistent with humiliation based on poverty; impartial welcome applies that duty without denying appropriate care for differing needs.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain Islamic teachings about divine unity faith and responsibility.
questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses tawhid in Islamic teaching?
options: Different gods govern separate parts of creation independently.
A ruler shares Allah’s divine status by holding office.
Worship is directed to Allah alone without partners.
An ancestor becomes divine through the number of descendants.
questions.answer: Worship is directed to Allah alone without partners.
questions.explanation: Tawhid affirms divine unity and excludes assigning partners to Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: In Surah al-Fatihah, the request for guidance follows praise and acknowledgement of dependence on Allah. What does this combination emphasise?
options: Guidance is unnecessary once praise has been offered.
Only material wealth is requested in the surah.
The worshipper claims complete independence from Allah.
Worship includes reliance on divine guidance.
questions.answer: Worship includes reliance on divine guidance.
questions.explanation: The surah brings praise, worship, seeking help and the request for guidance together.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Which classroom initiative best applies the emphasis on learning in Qur’an 96:1–5?
options: Helping learners read and understand while recognising the responsibility attached to knowledge.
Treating literacy as unnecessary because knowledge is never acquired.
Restricting books to a few pupils on the basis of family status.
Measuring knowledge only by public praise rather than understanding.
questions.answer: Helping learners read and understand while recognising the responsibility attached to knowledge.
questions.explanation: The passage associates reading and teaching with the Creator; the scenario applies that emphasis without reducing the verses to a school policy.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: A volunteer humiliates an orphan while claiming to honour Surah ad-Duha. Which aspect of the surah most directly contradicts this behaviour?
options: Its instruction to restrict all learning to adults.
Its instruction against harsh treatment of the orphan.
Its command that every gift be exchanged for money.
Its rule that only travellers deserve respectful speech.
questions.answer: Its instruction against harsh treatment of the orphan.
questions.explanation: The closing moral instructions include care in dealing with an orphan and a person asking for help.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Surah al-Kafirun rejects a proposed sharing of worship. Which conclusion best stays within that teaching?
options: Every disagreement requires personal abuse.
Distinct beliefs mean neighbours can never cooperate in ordinary matters.
Commitment to worship is not exchanged for a compromise of belief.
The surah instructs believers to worship every deity in turn.
questions.answer: Commitment to worship is not exchanged for a compromise of belief.
questions.explanation: The surah affirms distinct religious commitment; it does not prescribe insulting neighbours or alternating worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Surah an-Nas directs the seeker of refuge to Allah against
options: all forms of advice offered by other people.
only physical illness, without reference to inward influence.
the act of seeking guidance through prayer.
harmful whispering that can come through jinn or human beings.
questions.answer: harmful whispering that can come through jinn or human beings.
questions.explanation: The surah identifies the source of refuge and the danger of whispering, including human and jinn sources.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: A trader uses a balance that shows more than the actual weight supplied. Which principle in Qur’an 17:35 is violated?
options: Giving accurate measure and using a just balance.
Providing goods in response to a customer’s order.
Recording the date of a sale.
Explaining the price before payment.
questions.answer: Giving accurate measure and using a just balance.
questions.explanation: The verse requires fair measurement; a deliberately misleading balance defeats that requirement.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: A student publicly promises to return borrowed equipment but deliberately keeps it. Qur’an 61:2–3 most directly challenges
options: the use of equipment in a classroom.
the contradiction between professed words and deliberate conduct.
the practice of borrowing with permission.
the keeping of a written lending record.
questions.answer: the contradiction between professed words and deliberate conduct.
questions.explanation: The passage condemns declaring what one does not do.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: According to Qur’an 17:23–24, caring for ageing parents should include
options: mocking them when assistance takes time.
responding with contempt if they repeat a request.
respectful speech and compassionate treatment.
treating prayer for them as a reason to withhold all kindness.
questions.answer: respectful speech and compassionate treatment.
questions.explanation: The verses connect kindness, restrained speech, humility and prayer for parents.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: Qur’an 31:15 describes parents urging a child towards shirk. What balance does it teach?
options: Obey the demand because every parental instruction overrides faith.
Abandon all respectful conduct towards them.
Accept shirk privately while denying it publicly.
Do not obey that demand, but continue treating them kindly in worldly life.
questions.answer: Do not obey that demand, but continue treating them kindly in worldly life.
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes refusal of a wrongful religious demand from the continuing duty of good companionship.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: In Hadith terminology, what is the isnad?
options: The chain of people transmitting a report.
The textual content of the transmitted report.
The legal judgement drawn from applying a report.
The designation of a report as weak or sound.
questions.answer: The chain of people transmitting a report.
questions.explanation: The isnad identifies a report’s transmission chain; the matn is its textual content.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: A teacher separates the wording attributed to the Prophet from the names through whom it was reported. The wording is called the
options: isnad.
matn.
rawi.
sahih.
questions.answer: matn.
questions.explanation: Matn refers to the text of a report, distinguished from its chain of transmission.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: Two people perform the same outward charitable act for different purposes. An-Nawawi Hadith 1 draws attention especially to
options: the public similarity of the two actions alone.
only the number of spectators for each action.
their intentions.
the assumption that an outward deed reveals its entire purpose.
questions.answer: their intentions.
questions.explanation: The teaching makes motive central to the moral evaluation of action; appearance alone does not disclose it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: A learner wants useful revision materials for himself but hides the only shared copy from classmates. Which teaching of an-Nawawi Hadith 13 is most relevant?
options: Treating shared resources as private property once touched.
Assuming personal success requires every classmate’s failure.
Restricting all kindness to people who provide a reward.
Wishing comparable good for another as for oneself.
questions.answer: Wishing comparable good for another as for oneself.
questions.explanation: The hadith challenges self-centred standards of goodwill; the revision scenario is an original application.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: An unverified accusation arrives in a class discussion group. Which response best applies the speech principle in an-Nawawi Hadith 15?
options: Avoid spreading harmful claims and use speech responsibly.
Forward it privately because private sharing cannot cause harm.
Repeat it with a disclaimer while making no effort to check it.
Treat participation in every conversation as a duty regardless of content.
questions.answer: Avoid spreading harmful claims and use speech responsibly.
questions.explanation: The hadith links faith with beneficial speech or restraint; forwarding a damaging unverified claim does not fulfil that principle.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: After an insult, a player pauses instead of striking another player. This most directly applies an-Nawawi Hadith 16 through
options: denial that any disagreement occurred.
restraint of anger in conduct.
a claim that unfairness must never be reported.
a decision to punish everyone at the event.
questions.answer: restraint of anger in conduct.
questions.explanation: The counsel against anger calls for self-control, not a requirement to conceal or endorse wrongdoing.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: In an-Nawawi Hadith 18, good conduct is required
options: only when an audience can verify the person’s reputation.
only after a harmful deed has brought a visible penalty.
beyond situations where other people are watching.
only in formal acts of worship rather than ordinary relationships.
questions.answer: beyond situations where other people are watching.
questions.explanation: The hadith joins consciousness of Allah wherever one is with good deeds and good character towards people.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Which distinction between zakat and voluntary sadaqah is most accurate?
options: Zakat means any personal purchase; sadaqah means compulsory tax in every case.
Both terms always mean a payment only during Hajj.
Voluntary sadaqah cancels every zakat obligation automatically.
Zakat is a prescribed obligation under its conditions; voluntary sadaqah is additional giving.
questions.answer: Zakat is a prescribed obligation under its conditions; voluntary sadaqah is additional giving.
questions.explanation: The distinction concerns the prescribed obligation and additional voluntary charity, not an automatic substitution of one for the other.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Qur’an 2:183 associates fasting particularly with developing
options: taqwa, or consciousness of Allah.
a guarantee that abstention excuses dishonest speech.
the view that hunger itself cancels all other responsibilities.
public prestige as the sole measure of a fast’s value.
questions.answer: taqwa, or consciousness of Allah.
questions.explanation: The verse gives a moral and spiritual aim rather than merely describing abstention from food.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: In Qur’an 3:97, the obligation of pilgrimage is stated with reference to
options: only those already living in Makkah.
those able to undertake the journey.
only those who have completed Umrah first in a different year.
every individual without regard to capacity.
questions.answer: those able to undertake the journey.
questions.explanation: Ability is expressly relevant to the obligation; practical assessment of a person’s circumstances requires appropriate guidance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Tayammum differs from ordinary wudu principally because it involves
options: a purification made solely by washing with a larger amount of water.
a separate form of charity offered instead of ritual purity.
ritual purification using clean earth when its conditions apply.
a pilgrimage rite that replaces the need for purification.
questions.answer: ritual purification using clean earth when its conditions apply.
questions.explanation: Tayammum is an alternative mode of ritual purification under specified circumstances, not a replacement for worship as a whole.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: In early Islamic history, the Hijrah to Madinah refers to
options: the first revelation at Hira.
the Farewell Pilgrimage from Madinah to Makkah.
the journey known as al-Isra and al-Mi‘raj.
the migration from Makkah to Madinah.
questions.answer: the migration from Makkah to Madinah.
questions.explanation: The Hijrah is the migration that marks a major stage in the community’s development; it is distinct from revelation and other journeys.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders the first four caliphs in the standard Sunni historical account?
options: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali.
Umar, Abu Bakr, Ali, Uthman.
Uthman, Ali, Abu Bakr, Umar.
Ali, Uthman, Umar, Abu Bakr.
questions.answer: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali.
questions.explanation: The conventional sequence is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali; naming the account avoids implying identical evaluations across all traditions.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: The production of standard copies of the Qur’an under Caliph Uthman chiefly addressed a concern about
options: replacing the Arabic revelation with a new biography.
disputes and differences arising in recitation among expanding communities.
ending the use of written copies in favour of memory alone.
postponing every recitation until a new revelation arrived.
questions.answer: disputes and differences arising in recitation among expanding communities.
questions.explanation: The account in Sahih al-Bukhari describes concern over recitation differences and the preparation and distribution of copies.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain Islamic teachings about divine unity faith and responsibility.
questions.prompt: Why is publicly honouring a respected teacher different from treating that teacher as divine in Islamic belief?
options: Any expression of gratitude automatically makes a person divine.
Teaching gives a person independent divine power.
Respect for a person does not give that person a share in Allah’s divinity.
A large following removes the distinction between Creator and creature.
questions.answer: Respect for a person does not give that person a share in Allah’s divinity.
questions.explanation: Tawhid distinguishes ordinary human respect from attributing divinity or worship to a human being.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: What relationship between creation and learning is expressed in Qur’an 96:1–5?
options: Human knowledge is presented as wholly independent of any teaching.
The pen is mentioned only as a device for collecting tax.
Reading is presented as a substitute for acknowledging the Creator.
Allah is presented as Creator and the source of teaching.
questions.answer: Allah is presented as Creator and the source of teaching.
questions.explanation: The passage places the call to read alongside creation and teaching, including teaching by the pen.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Surah ad-Duha reminds its addressee of past divine care. How does the surah connect that reminder to conduct?
options: It follows reassurance with duties towards vulnerable people and acknowledgement of blessing.
It treats past hardship as permission to humiliate others.
It uses reassurance to cancel concern for people seeking help.
It makes gratitude depend on receiving praise from those helped.
questions.answer: It follows reassurance with duties towards vulnerable people and acknowledgement of blessing.
questions.explanation: The closing verses move from remembered care to obligations in speech and treatment of others.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: In Qur’an study, a surah is best described as
options: a verse within a chapter.
a chapter of the Qur’an.
a commentary explaining a Qur’anic passage.
a chain of transmitters attached to a report.
questions.answer: a chapter of the Qur’an.
questions.explanation: A surah is a Qur’anic chapter; the other descriptions concern different areas of study.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Qur’an 17:106 links the gradual revelation of the Qur’an with what manner of presenting it to people?
options: Withholding every part until no audience remained.
Replacing earlier revelation with a private commentary.
Recitation in portions at intervals.
Allowing each listener to compose a new surah.
questions.answer: Recitation in portions at intervals.
questions.explanation: The verse relates revelation in stages to reciting the Qur’an to people at a measured pace; gradual revelation is not the creation of a later text.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain Islamic teachings about divine unity faith and responsibility.
questions.prompt: Which description best distinguishes shirk from an ordinary mistake in arithmetic?
options: Shirk means any wrong answer on any subject.
Every calculation automatically constitutes worship.
Shirk is another name for the dawn prayer.
Shirk concerns associating partners with Allah, rather than every kind of error.
questions.answer: Shirk concerns associating partners with Allah, rather than every kind of error.
questions.explanation: The doctrinal term has a specific meaning and should not be extended to every unrelated error.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Explain Islamic teachings about divine unity faith and responsibility.
questions.prompt: In Qur’an 2:285, belief in the messengers is presented as part of
options: the believer’s confession of faith.
only an additional custom unrelated to belief.
a requirement to reject all messengers before Muhammad.
an entitlement to choose which messengers deserve belief solely by ethnicity.
questions.answer: the believer’s confession of faith.
questions.explanation: The passage links belief in Allah, angels, books and messengers; it does not treat earlier messengers as objects of hostility.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: Which conduct most directly contradicts Qur’an 2:42?
options: Correcting a mistaken statement after checking it.
Knowingly mixing truth with falsehood and hiding what is true.
Admitting that one does not know an answer.
Presenting an accurate record despite personal inconvenience.
questions.answer: Knowingly mixing truth with falsehood and hiding what is true.
questions.explanation: The verse addresses distortion and concealment of truth.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: A shopkeeper discovers that an assistant’s measuring container is too small. Which action best implements fair dealing?
options: Continue using it while displaying a religious slogan.
Blame customers for not bringing their own containers.
Replace or correct the measure and address customers’ shortfalls honestly.
Keep it for customers unlikely to complain.
questions.answer: Replace or correct the measure and address customers’ shortfalls honestly.
questions.explanation: The requirement of fair measurement calls for correcting the practice, not merely declaring honesty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: Qur’an 5:90–91 identifies which social danger associated with gambling?
options: A guarantee that every participant becomes wealthy.
The removal of every source of conflict.
Automatic fulfilment of obligations towards dependants.
Enmity and hostility among people.
questions.answer: Enmity and hostility among people.
questions.explanation: The passage associates gambling with conflict and distraction from remembrance and prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: A person cares for parents politely in public but habitually insults them at home. Which criticism follows from Qur’an 17:23–24?
options: Respectful treatment is an ongoing duty, not a public performance only.
Public courtesy makes all private mistreatment acceptable.
Financial provision always cancels the duty of respectful speech.
Only neighbours are entitled to gentle treatment.
questions.answer: Respectful treatment is an ongoing duty, not a public performance only.
questions.explanation: The verses describe the relationship with parents, including speech and compassion, rather than merely public appearances.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: Why is a long chain of names alone insufficient to establish that a Hadith is authentic?
options: Every long chain is automatically fabricated.
Transmission also requires critical assessment of continuity and narrators’ reliability.
The report’s text can never be examined.
A report becomes authentic when names are alphabetised.
questions.answer: Transmission also requires critical assessment of continuity and narrators’ reliability.
questions.explanation: Hadith criticism evaluates transmission and content through recognised criteria; counting names alone is inadequate.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: Which term commonly denotes a weak Hadith in the classification studied at this level?
options: Sahih.
Hasan.
Da‘if.
Matn.
questions.answer: Da‘if.
questions.explanation: Da‘if denotes weakness in classification; matn identifies a report’s text rather than its grade.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: Which pair of duties appears alongside responsible speech in an-Nawawi Hadith 15?
options: Completing Hajj and collecting every debt immediately.
Performing trade and refusing hospitality.
Studying genealogy and increasing personal rank.
Generosity towards the neighbour and guest.
questions.answer: Generosity towards the neighbour and guest.
questions.explanation: The hadith connects faith with speech, neighbourly generosity and hospitality.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: An-Nawawi Hadith 34 describes responses to wrongdoing in relation to
options: a person’s ability to act, speak or reject it inwardly.
the speaker’s popularity rather than capacity.
the assumption that inward disapproval is identical to public approval.
the requirement to use the same outward response in every circumstance.
questions.answer: a person’s ability to act, speak or reject it inwardly.
questions.explanation: The text distinguishes ability and modes of response. It should not be turned into unrestricted permission for coercion.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Which pairing correctly links an Islamic worship term with its basic meaning?
options: Zakat — the evening obligatory prayer.
Sawm — fasting.
Hajj — purification before daily prayer.
Wudu — fasting from dawn until sunset.
questions.answer: Sawm — fasting.
questions.explanation: Sawm refers to fasting; the other pairings confuse distinct terms.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Which of these is expressly named among the recipients of zakat in Qur’an 9:60?
options: Every wealthy person solely because of wealth.
Only relatives of the collector regardless of need or category.
People burdened by debt.
Only owners of shops that supply the collection office.
questions.answer: People burdened by debt.
questions.explanation: Debtors are among the listed categories; being wealthy, related or a supplier is not by itself a listed entitlement.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: What does Qur’an 2:184–185 provide for a person who is ill or travelling in relation to Ramadan fasting?
options: A command that no missed day can ever be made up.
An instruction that every traveller must abandon fasting permanently.
A rule that illness is never relevant to the obligation.
A concession involving making up days, under the stated conditions.
questions.answer: A concession involving making up days, under the stated conditions.
questions.explanation: The passage addresses illness and travel and completing the number of days; individual cases may require qualified guidance.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.subtopic: Purification prayer fasting charity and pilgrimage
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Why should studying the social purposes of zakat include the recipients as well as the giver?
options: The institution concerns support and distribution, not only the giver’s self-description.
Recipients have no role in the institution.
Only the giver’s public praise determines who is eligible.
Any recipient becomes responsible for paying the giver a profit.
questions.answer: The institution concerns support and distribution, not only the giver’s self-description.
questions.explanation: The stated recipient categories and distributive purpose make the receiving side essential to understanding zakat.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: Which distinction between compilation and standardisation of the Qur’an is most defensible?
options: Compilation is the first revelation, while standardisation is every later revelation.
Collecting material and preparing consistent authorised copies are related but different preservation activities.
Compilation and standardisation both mean translating the text into another language.
Compilation excludes written material, while standardisation excludes all recitation.
questions.answer: Collecting material and preparing consistent authorised copies are related but different preservation activities.
questions.explanation: The preservation accounts distinguish collecting written material from later preparation and distribution of standard copies.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: Why was migration to Madinah more than a change of geographical residence for the early Muslim community?
options: It removed every later difference or conflict within the community.
It made the earlier Makkan revelation no longer applicable.
It enabled the development of an organised communal life in a new setting.
It restricted communal obligations to those born in Madinah.
questions.answer: It enabled the development of an organised communal life in a new setting.
questions.explanation: The Hijrah’s significance includes community formation; it did not automatically remove all later challenges.
questions.textReference: Tarikh: Hijrah and formation of the Ummah

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret themes and lessons of prescribed Qur’anic passages.
questions.prompt: Explain how reassurance and social responsibility are connected in Surah ad-Duha. Develop four points with reference to Qur’an 93:3–11.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: The surah reassures its addressee against the idea of abandonment, establishing hope rather than despair. It recalls earlier vulnerability and divine care, so present security is understood in relation to past dependence. The prohibition of harsh treatment towards an orphan or a person asking for help turns that memory into obligations towards others. Acknowledging divine blessing provides a further response of gratitude; it should not be used as a justification for pride or humiliation of those in need.
questions.explanation: Credit other accurate, relevant explanations grounded in the specified text. Award each distinct idea once. The guide is original practice material, not an official examiner scheme.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Apply prescribed Qur’anic moral principles to clearly stated situations.
questions.prompt: Using Qur’an 17:23–24 and 31:15, explain how kindness to parents can coexist with refusing a demand that conflicts with tawhid. Develop four points.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: The duty of kindness includes considerate speech and care, especially as parents grow older. Compassion, humility and prayer for parents recognise the care received from them. A demand to associate partners with Allah is not obeyed, so parental authority is not presented as unlimited in matters of faith. Refusing that demand does not cancel good companionship in worldly life; disagreement over belief must not be made a pretext for contempt or neglect.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish Hadith components and interpret selected an-Nawawi traditions.
questions.prompt: Analyse the three areas of conduct linked with belief in an-Nawawi Hadith 15, and explain why outward politeness alone may be insufficient. Develop four points.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: Responsible speech requires beneficial words or restraint, so an attractive manner cannot justify spreading harmful falsehood. Generosity to a neighbour concerns practical treatment, such as considerate assistance, rather than a greeting followed by deliberate harm. Honouring a guest includes appropriate hospitality within one’s means, connecting belief with interpersonal responsibility. The three duties together require consistency between faith and conduct; public courtesy without truthful speech or consideration fails to fulfil the teaching.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish core worship concepts and their stated spiritual or social purposes.
questions.prompt: Explain four ways the prescribed distribution of zakat can serve spiritual and social purposes. Refer to Qur’an 9:60 and distinguish it from an unrestricted personal gift.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: For the giver under the relevant conditions, zakat is an obligation rather than merely a donation chosen for publicity. The categories include poor and needy people, directing support towards material hardship. Other stated categories, such as debtors and stranded travellers, show attention to differing forms of need rather than one identical circumstance. Allocation must respect the prescribed framework; this can restrain favouritism and differs from treating the entire fund as an unrestricted personal gift.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
questions.learningObjective: Identify purposes and significance of selected early Islamic developments.
questions.prompt: Explain four distinct aspects of Qur’anic preservation addressed by recording, memorisation, compilation and standard copying. Avoid treating these terms as interchangeable.
questions.answer: Indicative developed response: Recording preserves revelation in written material and provides evidence that can be gathered and checked. Memorisation preserves it through recitation and learning, complementing rather than being cancelled by writing. The compilation account under Abu Bakr describes a deliberate collection process associated with Zayd ibn Thabit and careful verification. The standard-copying account under Uthman addresses disagreements and the distribution of copies; it is a later preservation activity rather than a new revelation.
